entries.old: Whether this network/VLAN stays active when the gateway fails over to a UniFi LTE (cellular) backup WAN. Maps to the controller's `lte_lan_enabled` flag and only matters when a UniFi LTE failover device is in use; otherwise it is cosmetic. Defaults to `true` (network stays available during LTE failover); set to `false` to disable it while on the LTE backup link. The controller may set this automatically, which is why existing networks can show differing values.
entries.new: Whether this network/VLAN stays active when the gateway fails over to a UniFi LTE (cellular) backup WAN. Maps to the controller's `lte_lan_enabled` flag and only matters when a UniFi LTE failover device is in use; otherwise it is cosmetic. Set `false` to take the network off the LTE backup link. This is read back from the controller rather than defaulted: the controller sets it automatically, and a static `true` default stamped a network the controller held as `false` back to `true` on any plan that omitted the attribute.
entries.why_not_breaking: A description is not part of any configuration's contract: no config becomes invalid and no state migrates. The text is corrected because the released wording asserts a default the attribute no longer has, so keeping it would ship a statement known to be false about the behaviour shipping alongside it.

evidence.claim: The released schema documents a default that the candidate no longer declares.
evidence.source: provider-contracts/schema/terraform-1.15.8.json: lte_lan description says 'Defaults to `true`'; the candidate schema has no Default for lte_lan.

evidence.claim: Terraform never rejects a configuration on the basis of an attribute description.
evidence.source: Terraform plugin protocol semantics. Reasoning, not observation.
